selector.rationale: The patient's presentation with acute, severe precordial chest pain radiating to their left arm, accompanied by dyspnea, dizziness, and sweating, along with ECG findings of broad-based, asymmetrical, tall upright T waves in precordial leads V2 through V5 and subtotal occlusion of the proximal left anterior descending artery, best supports Acute Coronary Syndrome as the most comprehensive diagnosis.

rejected.label: Unstable Angina
rejected.why: Lack of specific evidence supporting Unstable Angina, such as prolonged chest pain at rest without evidence of myocardial necrosis.

rejected.label: Myocardial Infarction
rejected.why: Although some evidence supports Myocardial Infarction, the serum cardiac troponin I level was within the normal range, which contradicts this diagnosis.
